articles.title: Your mindfulness might determine whether venting helps or hurts your romantic relationship
articles.summary: Frequently discussing problems with a partner is often seen as a way to build closeness. But a new study suggests this habit is linked to worse relationship and sexual satisfaction for people who are highly mindful.

articles.title: The ethics of artificial intelligence in the life sciences: Universality, cultural diversity and an architecture of care
articles.summary: arXiv:2608.05436v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The life sciences and health research have started to benefit from artificial intelligence, which raises ethical concerns that are real but, we argue, not special. Any science should be governed by values that rest on how the human brain is built and socialised rather than anything distinct to artificial intelligence. Importantly, the human brain has a different, much less costly computational architecture than these machines. articles.title: Wearable ultrasound patch boosts REM sleep without drugs or surgery
articles.summary: A new wearable patch may help people reach REM sleep faster and remain there longer without medication or surgery. In a study of 28 participants, the device shortened the time to REM by 43 minutes and extended it by about 16 minutes. Researchers also observed signs of improved stress regulation and changes in brain circuits tied to emotion.

articles.title: Scientists discover a hidden brain shift that begins around age 50
articles.summary: Beginning around age 50, the brain’s memory center appears to lose many of its longtime immune cells and replace them with more inflammatory ones. This surprising shift may help explain how normal aging sets the stage for Alzheimer’s disease and dementia.

articles.summary: A recent study reveals that accumulated life knowledge helps adults manage their emotions across various situations, while fast mental processing speed is primarily linked to successfully reducing negative feelings like sadness and disgust.

articles.title: The link between vitamin intake and depression largely vanishes when factoring in lifestyle
articles.summary: While higher vitamin intake is often linked to better mental health, a new study reveals that this relationship mostly disappears once socioeconomic status, daily habits, and overall physical health are taken into account.

articles.title: THC medication made PTSD nightmares disappear for more than a third of patients
articles.summary: A prescription form of THC helped many people with PTSD escape recurring trauma-related nightmares, with more than one-third reporting that the nightmares disappeared completely after ten weeks. The results could point toward a long-awaited treatment for one of PTSD’s most distressing and stubborn symptoms.

articles.title: Nearly half of dementia cases may be linked to risks you can change
articles.summary: A long-term brain study found that common risks such as smoking, high blood pressure, heart disease, and high blood lipids were strongly linked to damage associated with vascular dementia. The findings suggest that healthier lifestyle choices could help delay dementia by reducing several harmful brain changes at once.

articles.title: Sitting up straight may improve your mood and decision-making
articles.summary: A simple change in posture may subtly affect how people feel and make decisions. Participants who sat upright reported greater feelings of pride and took more successful risks in a virtual balloon game than those who hunched over. Most did not realize researchers had influenced their posture, helping rule out the possibility that they were merely responding to expectations. The results suggest workplace ergonomics could influence more than physical comfort.

articles.title: Scientists discover the brain cells that keep you motivated
articles.summary: A group of brain cells called orexin neurons appears to help us keep working when reaching a reward becomes increasingly difficult. Blocking their activity weakened motivation in rats, pointing to a possible new target for understanding why people sometimes struggle to sustain goal-directed behavior.
